newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds expect trickle of new issues next week.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds expect trickle of new issues next week.

text.p: New issuance activity dried up on Friday, hit by holidays in most of Europe and little supply was mooted for next week, traders said.
In the fated lira-sector, Mexico is due to launch a 500 billion lira five-year FRN via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
It will be a benchmark for the borrower as the first lira-issue for Mexico and the first floating rate deal from an emerging market borrower.
Dealers said a spread in the low to mid-200 basis points over swaps was mooted, in line with where outstanding Latin American debt trades.
In the mainstream dollar sector, the Korea Development Bank (KDB) is expected to launch a $500 million global bond via J.P. Morgan and Merrill Lynch.
A syndicate official said no maturity had yet been decided, but traders expected one of five or 10-years.
Meanwhile banks were bidding for the mandate for an expected Eurobond from Spain's Instituto de Credito Oficial (ICO), new issues traders said.
They said the issue from the Spanish Government Development Bank, headquartered in Madrid, was likely to be launched in early December.
Euromarket expectations for a more imminent date was premature, dealers said.

ICO is expected to launch a Eurobond of up to $500 million guaranteed by the Kingdom of Spain. It is likely to mature after five years. Some traders said current price talk was in the region of 18 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and said Goldman Sachs were tipped as the lead manager for the transaction.
But a Goldman Sachs syndicate official said no mandate had yet been awarded.
